dave: Noticed small-request tail climb in nightly: host-side spend up ~9%. GPU profiles unchanged.
mira: Link to flame?
dave: https://perf.redwood/fg/3765 — big hotspots in pretokenize and resequencer alloc path.
toni: Perf snippet:
```
# perf top
  20.1% pretokenizer::scan_bytes
  13.6% resequencer::alloc_gap_buffer
  10.2% grpc::writev
```
sam: Looks like the reseq change that batches OOO fragments is causing per-frag mallocs + extra memcpys for short dialogs.
dave: Hypothesis: extra alloc+copy prevents small token keys from staying hot in KV cache, increases miss churn. Also many tiny writev syscalls.
mira: Quick mitigations: 1) reuse per-connection slab for reseq buffers, 2) aggregate small outgoing fragments for up to 2ms before writev.
dave: I prototyped slab reuse -> microbench: host p99 -7%, kv-hit +0.8%. Coalesce +2% but added jitter.
eng-bot: deploybot: pushed slab-reuse canary to canary-1 at 2026-03-22T11:00Z
toni: Can we add an "ingress_efficiency" EWMA to kernel selector so transient host noise doesn't flip us to small-batch kernels?
mira: Yes — soft signal only, plus a kernel-pin cooldown per session to avoid KV invalidation.
sam: I'll add a synthetic perf test that simulates 1-4 token bursts at high QPS to catch regressions in CI.
dave: Plan: land slab reuse today, toggle writev coalesce behind flag, add EWMA to selector, and canary. Expect final delta: small-chat p99 -9%, mixed -3%.
mira: Thanks — update RFC when ready.
